To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Parkin, the common fragile site locus FRA6E gene, has alterations in ovarian cancer and other tumor types.
Parkin is a large gene that spans the common fragile site FRA6E and that alterations in Parkin occur in ovarian, other tumor-derived cell lines, and primary tumors.
Parkin, the large gene located within FRA6E, is altered in a significant percentage of ovarian and nonovarian tumors and that Parkin may function as a tumor suppressor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning, characterization and analysis of the common fragile-site (CFS) genes FHIT, WWOX and Parkin.
the identification of the genes that reside in large common fragile sites.
the identification and characterization of genes that are located in the large CFSs and that are potentially involved in the development of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the common fragile site genes, FHIT, WWOX, and PARKIN are involved in the development, and/or progression of cancer.
Parkin is a tumor suppressor that is inactivated by mutation and/or deletion in ovarian cancer and possibly in many other types of cancer.

Parkin is a tumor suppressor candidate gene that is involved in the development/progression of ovarian and other cancers, and that it is also a major contributor to the etiology of Parkinson's disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Parkin is a tumor suppressor that is inactivated by a number of different mechanisms including deletion and/or rearrangement of exons.

the common fragile site genes, FHIT, WWOX and Parkin, are all tumor suppressor genes, and that the loss or alteration of these genes may play a critical role in the development and progression of a variety of different human cancers.
alterations in the common fragile sites, FHIT, WWOX and Parkin, occur in ovarian cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Parkin is a tumor suppressor that is inactivated in ovarian cancer.
the large CFS genes, Parkin, FHIT, and WWOX are all involved in cancer development and/or progression.

the common fragile site locus genes, Parkin, FHIT and WOX1, have similar genomic alterations in ovarian and nonovarian tumors, suggesting that the genomic instability at these sites may be a common mechanism in the pathogenesis and/or progression of a wide variety of human tumors.
